bio.summary: Adams is a sitting Boulder councilmember seeking the mayor’s office. She emphasizes climate resilience, affordability and a stronger policy role for council.

name: Fred Smith

bio.summary: Smith has run for Boulder council four times and is now a mayoral candidate. Known as “The Grateful Fred,” he proposes a local income tax on high earners, which would require a change in state law.

notes: Source availability is narrower than for questionnaire respondents; silence is not a policy position. The city elections page lists “Fred Smith,” while the official campaign-finance list calls the ballot name “Grateful Fred Instead” and records legal name Michael Smith: https://webapps.bouldercolorado.gov/election/report.php?electionID=25&report=candidateList .

bio.summary: Brockett is seeking another term as Boulder mayor, a role he has held since 2021. His campaign points to housing, homelessness, climate resilience and city finances.
bio.prior_office: Boulder mayor since 2021; city councilmember since 2015; previously Boulder Planning Board

bio.summary: Goldstein, also known as “Jamo,” is a first-time mayoral candidate and a CU Boulder student. His proposals include changes to housing taxation and ending the city’s Flock Safety camera contract.

name: Lisa Ann Jacobs

bio.summary: Jacobs is a 2026 Boulder mayoral candidate. Yellow Scene reported that she emphasized fiscal sustainability, litigation and transparency at an August candidate forum.

notes: No BRL individual profile, Better Boulder answer, DBP PDF, or verified campaign website located by September 24, 2026; do not infer positions on other issues. The city campaign-finance list marks her website “To be developed”: https://webapps.bouldercolorado.gov/election/report.php?electionID=25&report=candidateList . The city candidate-video showcase includes her introduction, but a transcript was not available here: https://vimeo.com/showcase/12421306 .

bio.summary: La Grave is an entrepreneur seeking the mayor’s office for the first time. He stresses government accountability, public safety and local economic activity.
Isaacson is again seeking a Boulder council seat after a previous campaign. Her stated priorities include housing affordability, climate resilience, city government and local businesses.
Winer is a sitting Boulder councilmember and mayor pro tem seeking reelection. She cites city services, streamlined processes and the local economy among her priorities.
bio.prior_office: Boulder city councilmember and mayor pro tem

bio.summary: Schuchard is a sitting Boulder councilmember seeking another term. He focuses on living costs, wildfire and climate resilience, and the effectiveness of city government.
Grano previously served on Boulder City Council and is running again. Her campaign focuses on middle-income housing, local economic activity and trust in city spending.
bio.years_in_boulder: first moved to Boulder in 2002; returned in 2007

bio.summary: Duran is a government consultant running for Boulder council. She emphasizes affordability, the local economy, wildfire preparedness and public safety.
Jamieson is a cybersecurity consultant seeking a Boulder council seat. His campaign focuses on code reform, fiscal oversight, housing and wildfire preparedness.

name: Lee Gilbert

bio.summary: Gilbert is an engineering consultant running for council for the first time. He focuses his campaign on reviewing major transportation projects, especially the Baseline corridor.

notes: Source availability is narrower than for questionnaire respondents; silence is not a policy position.

bio.summary: Marquis is a sitting councilmember seeking a second term. Her priorities include family housing, homelessness, wildfire resilience and accountable government.
bio.prior_office: Boulder city councilmember, elected 2023; previously BVSD school board

bio.summary: Richmond is a first-time council candidate and a diversity and education consultant. She advocates community-led governance, affordable housing and support for workers and small businesses.
Fuqua previously served on the Boulder Valley school board and is now seeking a council seat. He prioritizes affordable family housing, climate resilience and government transparency.
bio.prior_office: Boulder Valley School District board member

name: Lynn Segal

bio.summary: Segal is a retired ultrasonographer running for Boulder council. She advocates municipal ownership of utilities and seeks to reduce the university’s influence on development.

notes: Source availability is narrower than for questionnaire respondents; silence is not a policy position.

bio.summary: Martus is a first-time council candidate and a senior adviser with a background in institutional finance. He emphasizes budget oversight, government trust and changes to land-use regulation.
Rendleman is an attorney running for council for the first time. His stated priorities include wildfire preparedness, housing affordability and trust in city government.
